title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: One-day closure in a 7-day week; no past data, but logic applies 1/7th reduction to weekly sales.

drivers.name: Price increase (+2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior price hikes at same level led to 7–10 units (vs baseline 7.6), implying ~5–10% lift suppression; noise-adjusted estimate shrinks to -5%.

drivers.name: Thanksgiving holiday
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted effect is x1.0; past two occurrences show mixed results (x1.41, x0.97); insufficient evidence to override baseline.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.6. Thanksgiving (Thu) is a minor driver: past data shows x1.19 median vs baseline, but noise-adjusted effect is x1.0—evidence is weak. Store closure on Monday reduces demand: one day loss in a 7-day week implies ~14% reduction, but no past closure data. Price increase to $9.03 (+2.3%) likely suppresses demand; past price hikes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw 7–10 units (vs baseline 7.6), suggesting a slight drop. No promotion. Combined, drivers point to a modest decrease. Classical model gives 1.00, but judgment adjusts for closure and price. Final median adjusted down with uncertainty.

  events: Holiday: Thanksgiving (Thu)
  shelf price: 9.03 (+2.3% vs regular price 8.83)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 40.1 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 25.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
